hidden_target.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a lamellar dual-phase microstructure (approximately 71% L12 and 29% B2; B2 lamellae about 2–3 µm thick and containing nanoscale Cr-rich precipitates), polished to a mirror finish. Hot-rolled duplex stainless steel 2205 with approximately 52% austenite (γ-FCC) and 48% ferrite (δ-BCC) served as the comparator.
hidden_target.intervention: The study compared AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with DS2205 after three rapid heating/quenching cycles to approximately 1100 °C and during immersed reciprocating ball-on-flat tribo-corrosion against a 6.35 mm alumina ball. Sliding lasted 1800 s after 3600 s of open-circuit-potential stabilization; load was varied from 5 to 15 N and frequency from 3 to 9 Hz.
hidden_target.conditions: Tribo-corrosion was conducted in 100 mL deionized water at 25, 50, and 100 °C with a 3.5 mm stroke; the principal temperature comparison used 5 N and 5 Hz. Samples remained immersed for 300 s after sliding to monitor repassivation. Tests at 100 °C used a covered cell and reflux condenser. Thermal-shock conditioning was a transient high-heat-flux comparison, not an equilibrium-aging or continuous-service test.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: The HEA retained its fine L12/B2 lamellar structure after thermal shock and supported comparatively homogeneous Cr availability, robust passive-film repair, and a smaller, more stable wear track. The operative interfacial state changed with temperature: abrasive contact at 25 °C, a stable passive film and/or compacted tribo-layer with polishing wear near 50 °C, and discontinuous, repeatedly ruptured oxide/tribo-layer patches at 100 °C. DS2205 underwent substantial γ-to-δ redistribution and developed less mechanically stable films and more debris-assisted wear.
hidden_target.mechanism: Temperature changes the competition among sliding-induced depassivation, thermally activated repassivation, tribo-layer stability, abrasion, and corrosion. Near 50 °C, faster film repair without extensive brittle-film disruption produces a low-shear, polishing regime and minimizes wear. At 25 °C, slower or less-effective repair favors two-body abrasion; at 100 °C, repeated oxide/tribo-layer formation, fracture, and removal causes oxidative or third-body wear and greater friction instability. The HEA's stable dual-phase microstructure and robust passivation suppress severe abrasion and debris-driven degradation relative to DS2205.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to DS2205 under identical conditions, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is expected to retain its phase structure better and exhibit more stable passivation, lower coefficient of friction, smaller wear volume, and substantially lower tribo-corrosion wear rate. For both alloys, degradation is expected to be minimized near 50 °C rather than at 25 or 100 °C.
hidden_target.baseline: The primary baseline was duplex stainless steel 2205 tested and thermally conditioned identically. Within each alloy, 25 °C provided the room-temperature tribo-corrosion reference; as-cast phase fractions provided the pre-thermal-shock structural reference.
hidden_target.boundary: The conclusions hold for the tested 25–100 °C range, 5–15 N loads, 3–9 Hz reciprocation frequencies, 3.5 mm stroke, alumina counter-body, and controlled low-ionic-strength deionized water. They do not establish continuous-service stability at 1100 °C, equilibrium phase stability, oxidation kinetics, or performance in chloride-, sulfate-, or other ion-containing industrial waters.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: Wear volume and wear rate from white-light-interferometry wear-track metrology, coefficient of friction and open-circuit potential recorded during sliding and post-sliding repassivation, SEM wear-track morphology, EIS polarization behavior, EBSD phase fractions before and after thermal shock, XRD/EDS phase characterization, and potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
hidden_target.actual_result: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 retained nearly unchanged phase fractions after thermal shock (71% to 69% L12 and 29% to 31% B2, about 2% transformation), whereas DS2205 changed from 52% γ/48% δ to 17% γ/83% δ (about 35 percentage-point γ-to-δ transformation). Across all tested temperatures, loads, and frequencies, the HEA had approximately one order-of-magnitude lower and more stable wear rates than DS2205 and lower friction. At 5 N and 5 Hz, HEA mean COF values were 0.195 ± 0.012, 0.181 ± 0.015, and 0.254 ± 0.094 at 25, 50, and 100 °C, respectively, versus 0.403 ± 0.018, 0.315 ± 0.014, and 0.394 ± 0.021 for DS2205. Wear-volume loss followed 50 °C < 25 °C < 100 °C for both alloys. Morphology changed from two-body abrasion at 25 °C to minimum-wear polishing at 50 °C; at 100 °C the HEA showed patchy oxidative tribo-layer disruption, while DS2205 showed three-body abrasion and increased pile-up. The HEA also exhibited nobler, more stable OCP and higher polarization resistance than DS2205 at all tested temperatures.
